quiz.title: Chain Rule & Composite Functions Quiz (Ex 5.2)
quiz.intro: Eight questions on differentiating composite functions with the chain rule, straight from the ideas in Exercise 5.2. Pick an answer for each, then press Check my score.
quiz.about: NCERT Class 12 Maths, Continuity and Differentiability, Exercise 5.2

questions.q: What is the derivative of sin(x²)?
questions.explanation: By the chain rule, differentiate the outer sin to get cos(x²), then multiply by the derivative of the inner x², which is 2x. So the answer is 2x cos(x²).
The power rule gives 5(2x + 3)⁴, then multiply by the derivative of the inner 2x + 3, which is 2. That gives 10(2x + 3)⁴.

questions.q: What is the derivative of e^(sin x)?
questions.explanation: Differentiate the outer e^u to get e^(sin x), then multiply by the derivative of the inner sin x, which is cos x. The result is cos x · e^(sin x).

questions.q: Differentiate cos(3x) with respect to x.
questions.explanation: The derivative of cos is -sin, so we get -sin(3x), then multiply by the derivative of the inner 3x, which is 3. That gives -3 sin(3x).
Write it as (x² + 1)^(1/2). Its derivative is (1/2)(x² + 1)^(-1/2) times the inner derivative 2x, which simplifies to x / √(x² + 1).

questions.q: Differentiate sin(cos x) with respect to x.
questions.explanation: The outer derivative is cos(cos x); multiply by the derivative of the inner cos x, which is -sin x. The result is -sin x · cos(cos x).

questions.q: What is the derivative of tan(2x)?
questions.explanation: The derivative of tan u is sec² u, giving sec²(2x); multiply by the inner derivative of 2x, which is 2. That gives 2 sec²(2x).

questions.q: Differentiate (sin x)³ with respect to x.
questions.explanation: By the power rule the outer derivative is 3(sin x)²; multiply by the derivative of the inner sin x, which is cos x. The result is 3 sin² x cos x.

faq.q: What does Exercise 5.2 of Class 12 Maths cover?
faq.a: Exercise 5.2 sits inside the Continuity and Differentiability chapter and focuses on the chain rule — differentiating composite functions such as sin(x²), (2x + 3)⁵ and e^(sin x). You work from the outer function inward, multiplying by each inner derivative.

faq.q: How does the chain rule actually work?
faq.a: If y = f(g(x)), then dy/dx = f'(g(x)) · g'(x). In plain terms, differentiate the outermost function while leaving the inside untouched, then multiply by the derivative of the inside. Repeat this for every nested layer.

faq.q: What is the most common mistake in these problems?
faq.a: Forgetting to multiply by the inner derivative. Students often write the derivative of sin(x²) as cos(x²) and stop, missing the extra factor of 2x. Always finish by multiplying through by the derivative of the inside.

faq.q: How do I differentiate a function with several nested layers?
faq.a: Peel it one layer at a time. For sin(√x) you differentiate sin first, then √x, then x, and multiply all three results together. Working outside-in keeps the layers in order and avoids skipping a factor.
